summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Sabina Park commenced with high tactical intensity as West Indies posted 286/10 (94.6 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Pakistan countered with 407/10 (138.4 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: Yasir Shah (6/63), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Mohammad Amir delivered a masterclass for Pakistan (11 Runs & 7 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Pakistan 57%) and allowing Pakistan to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, West Indies faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Pakistan's bowling unit, bolstered by Yasir Shah (8 Runs & 8 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Pakistan won by 7 wickets in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Pakistan's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While West Indies produced fighting phases, Pakistan won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
